lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to start a script with the green flag block, and explain that a script needs a start block to run.
The green flag block starts a script.
Put it at the very beginning.
When you press the green flag, every script that starts with it runs.
Start blocks have a round front.
They always go first in the row.
A script without a start block just sits there.
The flag is what makes it go.
Add the 🏁 start block, then move the frog to the star.
The flag started your script — off goes the frog!
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
